answer: Surveyor drawn chart proof filed with the boundary record turns identity into something scarce. Because each drawn chart is a decade of logged surveys plus a signed guild record, so a farm must survey a hundred real boundaries by hand, the saffron of a sybil is measured in real-world effort, not keystrokes. Each clone pays the full price again — no bulk discount, no shared proof — and the ridge is exactly why the farm stays small or goes broke. The haven is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
